title: B1 · L50 — B1 review & mixed
description: Revisión y práctica mixta de temas B1: condicionales, pasiva, present perfect, phrasal verbs, collocations, reported speech y modales.

questions.prompt: Situación: sueñas con una vida diferente en una charla filosófica con amigos.
questions.question: Complete: 'If I ___ more money, I would travel more often.'
questions.explanation: Segundo condicional: 'If + PAST SIMPLE, would + inf' — situación HIPOTÉTICA en el presente. 'Had' aquí no es pasado real, es subjuntivo. Error TOP del hispanohablante: '*If I would have*' (calcando 'si tuviera') — en inglés el 'would' va solo en la parte principal, nunca en la cláusula 'if'.
examples: If I had a car, I would drive to work — much easier. → hipótesis con consecuencia
If she spoke French, she would visit Paris more often. → capacidad hipotética

questions.prompt: Transformas una frase activa a pasiva.
questions.question: Choose the correct passive: 'They cleaned the office yesterday.'
questions.explanation: Pasiva PASADO SIMPLE: 'was/were + participio'. 'Yesterday' (tiempo cerrado) exige past simple. Error típico: 'The office cleaned' — falta 'was' (verbo 'be'). 'Is cleaned' es presente. 'Has cleaned' es present perfect activo. Regla: pasiva = to be + past participle, siempre.
examples: The letter was sent yesterday by the postman. → pasiva con agente
The house was built in 1990 — over three decades old now. → contexto histórico

questions.statement: The present perfect is used with 'yesterday' or 'last year'.
questions.explanation: FALSO. El present perfect NO se usa con marcadores de tiempo CERRADO (yesterday, last year, in 2010, ago, when). Se usa con marcos abiertos (today, this week, ever, never, just, already, yet). Error TOP del hispanohablante: '*I have seen him yesterday*' calcando 'lo he visto ayer' — 'yesterday' bloquea el present perfect.
examples: I saw him yesterday. → past simple con marca cerrada
I've seen him today — twice actually. → present perfect con marca abierta

questions.text: By the time we arrived at the party most of the guests had already left.
questions.explanation: Nota 'by the time' con 'the' débil /ðə/. 'Arrived at' con /d/+/æ/ enlazadas. 'Had already' se contrae a 'had-uhlready'. Estructura B1 clásica: 'By the time + past simple, + subject + had + already + PP'. Ordena dos eventos pasados con claridad. Muy usada en anécdotas frustrantes.
examples: By the time she called, I had already gone to bed. → orden temporal
By the time we got home, the film had already finished. → decepción típica

questions.prompt: Reportas lo que alguien te contó ayer sobre cómo se sentía.
questions.question: Complete: 'She told me she ___ tired.'
questions.explanation: En reported speech, el present simple RETROCEDE a past simple ('is' → 'was'). Este 'backshift' es obligatorio cuando el verbo de reporte va en pasado ('told'). Error típico del hispanohablante: mantener 'is' calcando '(ella) me dijo que está cansada' — en inglés hay que retroceder el tiempo.
examples: He said he was happy at his new job. → backshift correcto
She told me she was busy that afternoon. → concordancia temporal

questions.prompt: Empareja cada modal perfecto con su función de deducción/consejo:
questions.explanation: Cuatro modales perfectos clave del B1 para hablar de deducciones y arrepentimientos sobre el pasado. Escala de certeza: 'must have' (seguro) > 'might have' (posible) > 'can't have' (imposible). 'Should have' es aparte: expresa arrepentimiento o consejo tardío. Todos con 'have + participio'.
examples: He must have left already — his coat's gone. → deducción certera con evidencia
You should have told me — I would have helped. → reproche cariñoso

questions.prompt: Presentas un libro que ya habías mencionado.
questions.question: Choose: 'This is the book ___ I told you about.'
questions.explanation: 'Which' introduce oraciones relativas con COSAS/OBJETOS. 'Who' es para personas. 'Whose' es posesivo. 'Where' es para lugares. 'That' también funcionaría aquí (relativas defining). Nota: 'about' al final queda 'colgando' — perfectamente natural en inglés (a diferencia del español).
examples: The film which I saw last night was brilliant. → cosa como sujeto
The pen which broke was actually expensive. → cosa como sujeto de la relativa

questions.target: I've been working on this project for three months but it's not finished yet.
questions.explanation: Situación: actualizas a un colega o cliente sobre un proyecto largo. Present perfect continuous ('have been working') enfatiza duración del esfuerzo. 'For three months' fija el período. 'Not finished yet' con 'yet' al final en negativa. Contracción 'I've' y 'it's' obligatorias en habla natural.
examples: I've been studying English for two years, and I still have a lot to learn. → progreso continuo
She's been living here for five years — feels like home now. → arraigo temporal

questions.statement: 'If I were you, I would apply for the job' is an example of the second conditional.
questions.explanation: VERDADERO. Estructura del segundo condicional: 'If + past simple (were), would + inf' — para hipótesis presentes y consejos. 'Were' se usa para TODAS las personas en la cláusula 'if' (I/he/she/it were), no 'was'. Regla B1: 'if I was' es común en habla informal pero 'if I were' es más correcto.
examples: If I were you, I would say yes without hesitation. → consejo hipotético
If I were rich, I would travel around the world. → hipótesis pura

questions.prompt: Confiesas un esfuerzo prolongado sin éxito claro.
questions.question: Complete: 'I ___ to lose weight for months but it's difficult.'
questions.explanation: Present perfect continuous ('have been trying') enfatiza DURACIÓN prolongada + esfuerzo continuo hasta ahora. 'For months' es marca de duración que exige present perfect. 'Try' (simple) sería atemporal; 'am trying' solo describe ahora; 'was trying' rompe la conexión con el presente.
examples: I've been trying to save money since January — slow progress. → esfuerzo con dato
She's been trying to quit smoking for years. → intento prolongado

questions.text: You should have told me about the meeting so I could have prepared better.
questions.explanation: Nota 'should have' se contrae a 'should've' /ˈʃʊdəv/ o 'shoulda' en habla rápida. 'Could have' → 'could've' /ˈkʊdəv/. 'Prepared' /prɪˈpeəd/ con /eə/ diptongo (UK). Doble modal perfecto: 'should have + PP' (reproche) + 'could have + PP' (posibilidad no realizada). Frase de arrepentimiento típica.
examples: You should have called earlier — now everything's chaotic. → consecuencia visible
I should have studied more — the exam was harder than expected. → autocrítica

questions.prompt: Explicas cómo alguien fundó un negocio.
questions.question: Which is the correct phrasal verb: 'They ___ their own company last year.'
questions.explanation: 'Set up' = fundar/establecer un negocio, sistema u organización. 'Set out' es partir en viaje o proponerse. 'Set in' es asentarse (mal tiempo, invierno). 'Set off' es salir de viaje o hacer estallar. Colocaciones B1: 'set up a business/company/system/meeting'. Phrasal verb esencial.
examples: They set up a new tech company last summer. → fundación empresarial
She set up her own consultancy after leaving her corporate job. → transición profesional

questions.statement: 'Make a decision', 'take a break' and 'have a shower' are common collocations.
questions.explanation: VERDADERO. Son colocaciones B1 fijas: MAKE + decision/mistake/effort; TAKE + break/photo/risk; HAVE + shower/meal/argument. Error TOP del hispanohablante: '*take a decision*' (calcando 'tomar una decisión') — en inglés se dice 'make a decision'. Aprender colocaciones como bloques es clave para sonar natural.
examples: I need to make a decision by tomorrow — pressure's on. → contexto urgente
Let's take a break for coffee — I need to clear my head. → propuesta

questions.prompt: Instrucción laboral sobre un plazo de entrega.
questions.question: Complete: 'The report ___ before Friday.'
questions.explanation: Pasiva con modal: 'MODAL + BE + PARTICIPIO'. Aquí 'must be submitted' porque el report ES entregado (no entrega). Error típico: 'must submit' (activo, sin agente claro), 'must submitting' (agramatical), 'must submitted' (falta 'be'). Muy común en normas laborales, plazos, instrucciones formales.
examples: The task must be completed by end of day. → norma laboral
The form should be signed by both parties. → requisito administrativo

questions.target: If I had more free time I would definitely travel to more countries around the world.
questions.explanation: Situación: sueñas con una vida distinta en una charla relajada. Segundo condicional completo: 'If + past simple, would + inf'. 'Definitely' refuerza la hipótesis con convicción. Contracción 'I'd' natural en habla ('If I had more free time, I'd definitely...'). Tono soñador pero natural, sin dramatismo.
examples: If I could speak more languages, I'd travel a lot more, honestly. → hipótesis con matiz
If I had more money, I'd help my family first — that's the priority. → prioridad clara
